{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of vendor-form Master Services Agreement
**Status:** All findings below are verified (verification: pass)

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and identified **10 issues** requiring action (7 deviations and 3 missing clauses) against **8 clauses that already meet our position**.

The commercial architecture of the draft is unbalanced in three ways:

- **The risk-allocation package is incomplete.** There is no indemnification provision anywhere — the numbering jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and the absent Section 20 leaves dangling cross-references in Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5. There is also no termination-for-convenience right and no transition-assistance or data-return obligation. Each of these sits in walk-away territory, and we have inserted clauses at the preferred position.
- **Several one-way restrictions bind us rather than Vendor.** Section 2.1 (three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights), Section 7.2 (right of first refusal plus an MFN matching obligation running against us), and Section 12.4 (24-month post-term non-compete and 24-month no-hire) all fail the fallback on multiple material terms. Notably, each of these directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, minimum-volume, most-favoured-customer or no-hire commitment — so the redlines also cure internal inconsistency.
- **Ownership and forum are wrong.** Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us with only a revocable, term-limited licence back, and Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts while Section 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the New York County courts.

On the positive side, the limitation of liability (Section 21), assignment and change of control (Section 24), licence grant (Section 13), audit rights (Section 22), renewal mechanics (Section 8), warranties (Section 19) and Vendor insurance (Section 18) all meet our preferred position, and there are no liquidated damages or termination penalties payable by us. Those clauses are not redlined.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 19.5 (gap where Section 20 should sit; cross-referenced at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4) |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4) |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 2.1 (see also §§ 7.1, 27.3) |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.3) |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 |
| 9 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 |
| 10 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination) |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Deviation | § 2.1 |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (see also § 16.5) |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and must be resolved before signature:

| Rule | Section | Why it is walk-away | Our position |
|---|---|---|---|
| INDEMN | Missing Section 20 | No Vendor IP indemnity at all; the absent Section 20.5 IP remedies are already cross-referenced in § 9.3 | Insert a new Section 20 at the preferred position: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; customary exclusions; procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (restoring § 20.5); notice, control and cooperation procedure; and a Customer indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. No super-cap needed because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims. |
| T4C | § 9 | No convenience exit for us in a three-year term, compounded by § 2.1's take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" | Insert a new § 9.4: Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, expressly overriding § 2.1, and confirm Vendor has no convenience right during a term. |
| MINCOMMIT | § 2.1 | Multi-year take-or-pay (USD 2,000,000/year for three years) with no reduction or termination right; contradicts §§ 12.3 and 7.1 | Remove the minimum commitment; fees payable for usage or ordered Services only. Fallback: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised. |
| EXCLUSIVITY | § 7.2 | De facto right of first refusal on our sourcing, with no service-category limit, no 12-month sunset and no performance-based exit; contradicts § 12.3 | Remove the exclusivity / first-refusal gate on engaging another provider. |
| MFN | § 7.2 | MFN runs the wrong way (against us) and is unbounded as to product line, time and comparison carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3 | Delete the disclose-and-match obligation imposed on Customer. |
| NONCOMPETE | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term non-compete, any competing product or service, any territory, and expressly bars acquisitions; contradicts § 12.3 | Delete. Fallback offered in comment: a narrowed restriction tied to a specific Vendor product if protection is genuinely needed. |
| NOSOLICIT | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire covering every Vendor employee, expressly overriding general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3 | Narrow to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, measured from the end of an individual's involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and the no-hire element deleted. |
| GOVLAW | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts — outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) — and inconsistent with § 28.2 | Replace with New York law and defer venue to the New York County courts already named in § 28.2. §§ 28.3 escalation and the interim-injunctive-relief carve-out are acceptable and left intact. |
| TRANSITION | § 10.1 | No obligation to return or export Customer Data in usable form; § 16.5 defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15", but Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 covers only processing limitations and privacy compliance | Insert new § 10.3: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, Customer Data return in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion. Fallback of 90 days' assistance offered in the comment. |

**Critical deviation outside the walk-away list.** § 14.2 (IP) gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for us (as defined in § 1.4), leaving us only a revocable, non-transferable licence for the Order Form term. That fails both the preferred position and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense), and the § 13.2 perpetual licence pulled in by § 14.3 does not cure it because it is limited to software and Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable. Our redline reverses ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment, while preserving Vendor's ownership of Vendor Technology under §§ 14.3/13.2. §§ 14.1 and 14.4 are satisfactory and unchanged.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm the commercial mandate on § 2.1.** The take-or-pay is the largest single exposure and interacts with the missing convenience right. We need business sign-off on whether any minimum is acceptable before we table the fallback (12-month term, 30-day reduction right, true-up not penalty).
2. **Send the redline with the four inserted/restored provisions** — Section 20 (Indemnification, including § 20.5 IP remedies), § 9.4 (Customer termination for convenience), § 10.3 (transition assistance and certified data return) and the § 14.2 ownership reversal. These are the items that cannot be closed by deletion alone.
3. **Table the deletions as a single package**, framed on internal consistency: §§ 7.2, 12.4 (non-compete) and 12.4 (no-hire) each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3. We expect limited resistance on that basis, and we hold the narrowed non-solicit and specific-product non-compete as fallbacks.
4. **Conform § 28.1 to § 28.2** (New York law and New York County venue) as a drafting-consistency point rather than a negotiation, given the existing conflict in the draft.
5. **Confirm no further amendment to the compliant clauses.** We will not reopen §§ 8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22 or 24. Two minor points are noted for the record only and are not being redlined: the "Fees" definition in § 1.5 excludes a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form states otherwise (immaterial given the USD 1,000,000 cap floor), and § 14.2's revocability tension is addressed through the IP redline rather than the licence rule.
6. **Request insurance certificates** under § 18.2 at signature, consistent with the existing clause.
"}
